title: Test headless Codex, OpenCode and Claude single-Action runs (experiment fixture)
problem: Agents cannot run the Codex, OpenCode or Claude Code CLIs: they fail inside the agent sandbox and launching unsandboxed agents is refused. So nobody knows which headless provider sessions, started with the unattended command line Arcadia's launcher builds for a standing-policy launch, can finish one trivial governed Action with no human input. A fingerprint launch today runs the interactive TUI, which never exits, so this has to be proved by running each provider for real, on a disposable fixture, as the operator.
desired_effect: For each of Codex, OpenCode and Claude Code, independently and in that order, on its own fresh Decision 0082 experiment workspace and one-Action fixture repository (no remote) under a temporary directory (the workspace lives in $TMPDIR, not workspaces/exp-*, because Codex's workspace-write sandbox can write the temp directory but not the workspaces directory, and everything is disposable and removed afterwards), Arcadia prepares the Action (go --apply --agent <provider> with a seeded immutable build packet and a fresh experiment-only heartbeat) on the provider's start-tier model (the light tier: gpt-6-luna for Codex, haiku for Claude Code, the light opencode model), then the script runs the provider headless with the exact unattended argv Arcadia's shipped launch builder produces (codex exec --json --model ... --sandbox workspace-write --cd <worktree> <brief>; opencode run --model ... <brief>; claude --print --output-format stream-json --verbose --permission-mode acceptEdits --settings <per-session file> --setting-sources "" --model ... <brief>) for at most 15 minutes each, teeing its output to a log. For Claude Code the per-session settings file's allow list covers the fixture's registered validation command (node scripts/check-fixture.mjs) and arcadia agent-ask draft, and the run refuses if it does not. It prints and records one PASS/FAIL/SKIPPED table covering every provider: the provider exited 0 within the cap (and, for Claude, its stream-json result event is not is_error), MARKER.md has the exact expected line, node scripts/check-fixture.mjs passes, a clean commit with the exact file exists on the candidate branch (when the agent could not commit, as Codex's workspace-write sandbox denies Git's index.lock and Claude Code's headless allow list has no commit, the script plays the host's role afterwards with arcadia preserve's own code, then judges the commit), and a criterion-complete completion Agent Ask was drafted (preview accepts it) or settled by the agent itself (the Action is complete in the experiment database, the archived Ask's candidate revision is an ancestor of HEAD holding the exact file, and the tree is clean). Each failed criterion carries the first relevant error lines from that provider's log (permission denied, auto-rejecting, sandbox, Operation not permitted, an is_error result event) in the receipt's failureDetails, so a failure can be diagnosed from the receipt alone. It also reports the model used per provider, whether the worktree's gitdir lies inside Codex's sandbox-writable roots and, as information only, what session reconcile makes of the finished Session (accepted_completion is unreachable in an experiment workspace because no worker exists). Every selected provider is tried, whatever the others do; a provider whose precondition (binary, sign-in, headless flags) is missing is SKIPPED with the reason and the others still run. Run it from /runs, or from a terminal: /Users/pmark/Dev/MR/Arcadia/arcadia/artifacts/generated/operator-scripts/test-headless-provider-single-action.sh run Expected duration: typically 5 to 25 minutes, at most about 50. Cost: uses your existing Codex, OpenCode and Claude Code plans on their light-tier models; no separate spend. The receipt reports the agent part and the host part separately, so an agent-only pass is visible: PASS means the agent committed; PASS (agent + host preservation) means the host step committed; PASS (agent); host preservation not exercised means the agent did everything but the host step could not run in an experiment workspace.
preconditions: Run on the operator's own Mac, signed in. Each provider's preconditions are checked separately and a missing one SKIPS only that provider: codex on PATH with codex login status succeeding; opencode on PATH with opencode auth list showing a credential (an uncertain answer warns and proceeds); claude on PATH with claude auth status --json reporting loggedIn (or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN set in the environment). Each installed CLI must also carry the headless flags the launch passes. The run is refused only when no selected provider can run
Today is within Decision 0082's experiment window (through 2026-10-18)
The Arcadia checkout this library belongs to has its dependencies installed (the test runs its CLI)
No other input is needed; nothing is read from or written to the live workspace except a read-only leak-check snapshot

Where it works: the experiment workspace, fixture and candidate worktree live in a temporary directory under $TMPDIR (not workspaces/exp-*), so the provider's sandbox can write them; the scripts' logs and receipt stay in runs/<timestamp-pid>/

parameters.--keep: Optional argument (terminal only; /runs passes none), or ARCADIA_HEADLESS_TEST_KEEP=1: keep the temporary experiment workspace, fixture and candidate worktree for inspection. The run logs and receipt are always kept.
parameters.--providers: Optional argument (terminal only), or ARCADIA_HEADLESS_TEST_PROVIDERS: a comma-separated subset of codex,opencode,claude to try, in the order given (default: codex,opencode,claude).
parameters.--model-codex / --model-opencode / --mod: Optional arguments (terminal only), or ARCADIA_HEADLESS_TEST_MODEL_CODEX / _OPENCODE / _CLAUDE: the model to start that provider on (default: the start-tier model). Written to the experiment workspace's own coding-agent-models config, never the live workspace's.
parameters.ARCADIA_HEADLESS_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS: Optional environment variable: the per-provider cap in milliseconds (default 900000, fifteen minutes).

expected_duration: Typically 5 to 25 minutes. At most about 50 minutes: one 15-minute provider cap for each of Codex, OpenCode and Claude Code, plus about a minute of setup per provider.
cost_note: Uses the operator's existing Codex, OpenCode and Claude Code plans: one short headless session each, on the light-tier model, on a one-line task. No API key is read or entered and no separate spend is authorized or incurred.

does: Checks each selected provider's preconditions separately (binary on PATH, sign-in, and the headless flags the installed CLI must carry) and SKIPS a provider whose precondition is missing, with the reason, while the others still run; refuses before creating anything only when today is outside Decision 0082's experiment window (through 2026-10-18) or no selected provider can run. OpenCode is skipped only when opencode auth list clearly shows no credentials (an uncertain answer warns and proceeds)

Creates a temporary directory, a fresh experiment workspace per provider in it with arcadia init --profile experiment, and a one-Action fixture repository with no remote under that workspace's projects directory; every Arcadia command names that workspace explicitly and the live workspace is never addressed. The fixture registers node scripts/check-fixture.mjs as its Project's declared validation command, which is what puts it in Claude Code's per-session allow list

Writes a freshly timestamped worker heartbeat file inside the experiment workspace only (the experiment guard forbids starting a worker), seeds one immutable build packet there, and prepares the candidate worktree with go --apply through a recording process boundary that starts nothing. An operator model override is written to that experiment workspace's own config/coding-agent-models.json

Runs each provider CLI headless with the unattended argv the shipped launch builder produces for go --launch, in the candidate worktree, with ARCADIA_WORKSPACE set in the provider's own environment to the experiment workspace (never exported in any shell) and the operator-script markers removed, for at most 15 minutes each, killing its whole process group on timeout. The provider process is not confined to the fixture beyond what the provider enforces: Codex runs with --sandbox workspace-write and Claude Code with acceptEdits and a narrow per-session allow list (the fixture check, the Ask draft in its arcadia and pnpm arcadia spellings, and the Agent tool that lets it call in a larger model of its own provider within its existing plan; --setting-sources is empty so no ambient settings widen it), but OpenCode runs unsandboxed with its ambient permission configuration, so a misbehaving OpenCode could write anywhere the operator can; the 15-minute cap and process-group kill bound it, and the fixture holds nothing of value

Lets go --launch run its ordinary provider capacity probe, which for Codex is a real, read-only codex app-server account/rateLimits/read query against the operator's own Codex account, and which refreshes the local coding-agent telemetry cache under ~/.arcadia/telemetry (the one Arcadia-side write outside the temporary directory and runs/<timestamp-pid>/)

Takes a read-only live-workspace leak-check snapshot before and after. Other sessions legitimately write the live workspace, but Decision 0082 stops experiments at any experiment-caused write, so any difference other than the Codex trust entry is logged and receipted as LIVE WORKSPACE CHANGED: attribute before any further experiment, as a possible Decision 0082 stop condition

Writes run.log, one log per provider, a receipt.json (arcadia-operator-run-receipt-v1 with per-provider results, models, failure details and log paths) and, when no provider passed, a failure-handoff.md under runs/<timestamp-pid>/, which are always kept
Removes the temporary directory at the end unless --keep or ARCADIA_HEADLESS_TEST_KEEP=1 is given

Lets the providers write their own normal session and state directories (for example under ~/.codex, ~/.claude and ~/.local/share/opencode), as any run of them does; the script itself never reads or edits them. Codex also persists a project-trust entry, [projects."<fixture repo>"] trust_level = "trusted", to ~/.codex/config.toml for a new project directory, and Claude Code may record its own trust or session state under ~/.claude. The Decision 0082 leak check reports the Codex entry as a changed hashes.codexConfig, which is reported as Codex trust entry (operator ruled 2026-10-09: not a stop condition) and not acted on; any other leak-check change (including a Claude trust or settings hash) is still reported as a possible Decision 0082 stop condition for the operator to attribute. To stop the experiment touching host config, the test passes Codex a per-invocation --config trust override (projects."<path>".trust_level="trusted") for exactly its own fixture repository and candidate worktree; whether Codex then skips the write is unverified until a run's leak check

After a provider exits and its Session is reconciled, if the candidate is the exact MARKER.md left uncommitted beside a drafted Ask, runs arcadia preserve's own code (runPreserveCommand, the code the worker runs) on that experiment candidate: its manual-handoff path, which authorizes local preservation only (validation under Seatbelt in the temp dir, then a local commit), with no remote, push or pull request. It may refuse in an experiment workspace; that is reported, not forced. A step that ran and refused is reported as host_failed, one that could not run here as not_exercised, and a step that committed and then errored as preserved

Gives OpenCode, and only OpenCode, a per-process OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT permission grant (external_directory allow) for the temporary tree this test created, because OpenCode's non-interactive run auto-rejects permission prompts and its first tool call in the macOS temporary directory was refused (run 20261009T135444Z-90379); the operator's ~/.config/opencode is never read for this or written
never_does: Never addresses, reads for any purpose but the leak-check snapshot, or writes the live martianrover workspace, never exports ARCADIA_WORKSPACE, never reads the live workspace's Claude Code token file, and gives the provider an arcadia shim that pins the experiment workspace and refuses to fall back to the default

Never activates production, starts, stops or restarts a service or worker, installs the go-broker, or merges, pushes or opens anything on GitHub, and never settles anything in the live workspace (the provider may settle its own completion Ask, but only inside the experiment workspace)

Never reads, edits or repairs provider global configuration or authentication (codex login, opencode auth login, claude auth login and their config files stay the operator's; the providers' own session and state directories are the only provider-side writes, made by the providers), and never installs software or enters a credential
Never registers a repository with a remote, and never touches the primary Arcadia checkout, other worktrees or any path outside its temporary directory and runs/<timestamp-pid>/
Never reports accepted_completion: with no worker in an experiment workspace it cannot be reached, so session reconcile output is information only

Never pushes, opens a pull request or touches a remote during the host step, and never runs the worker's leased preservation path with production authority; an experiment workspace cannot hold that authority

success.effect: At least one provider exited 0 within the cap, wrote and committed the expected MARKER.md, passed the fixture check and drafted a criterion-complete completion Agent Ask that preview accepts. The receipt records, for every provider, PASS, FAIL or SKIPPED, the model used, the table, the exact command, the log paths, the failure details of any failed criterion and the gitdir finding. The receipt separates agentPart from hostPart and records passKind (agent, agent_and_host, agent_host_failed or agent_only). The script exits 0.
success.next: Read receipt.json under runs/<timestamp-pid>/ in the operator-scripts directory. Each provider that passed is viable headless on this host for a standing-policy launch; give the receipt (especially the gitdir finding) to Arcadia to decide the next Action. For each provider that failed, failureDetails holds the failed criterion and the first relevant lines of its log; for each skipped provider, reason names the missing precondition. If the receipt's liveWorkspaceSnapshot.otherChanges is not empty, attribute every change (other sessions versus this experiment) before any further experiment; an experiment-caused write is a possible Decision 0082 stop condition. liveWorkspaceSnapshot.codexTrustEntry set means only Codex's project-trust entry changed, which the operator ruled on 2026-10-09 is not a stop condition. Read hostPart: agent_only means the agent's work is proven but host preservation (the worker's commit step) still needs a real exercise, which an experiment workspace cannot give.

failure.effect: No provider passed every criterion, or the run was refused (the experiment window closed, or no selected provider can run). The script exits non-zero and writes receipt.json and failure-handoff.md with the table and the failing criterion for each provider, with the first relevant error lines from each provider's log, plus every provider log. Nothing outside the temporary directory and the run directory was changed.
failure.next: Give failure-handoff.md, run.log and the provider logs to a coding agent to diagnose the first failing criterion of each provider (the receipt's failureDetails already carries the first error lines from the log). A skipped provider names its precondition: sign in (codex login, opencode auth login or claude auth login), put the binary on PATH, upgrade a CLI that lacks the headless flags, or note that Decision 0082's window closed. Rerun with --keep from a terminal to inspect the fixture, or --providers <name> to rerun one provider. If the log says LIVE WORKSPACE CHANGED, attribute the change before any further experiment. A Codex or Claude candidate left uncommitted is expected (Codex's sandbox denies Git's index.lock; Claude's headless allow list has no commit); the host step or the agent-only fallback should cover it, so a FAIL on the commit criterion means something else is wrong.
